Fucosylation and sialylation distribution

plot_fuc_sia_pie.Rd

Classify glycans using only their composition and pool all samples.

Usage

plot_fuc_sia_pie(x, weight = "equal", ...)

Arguments

x

A glyexp::GlycomicSE() or glyexp::GlycoproteomicSE() with glycan_composition row annotations. Legacy glyexp_experiment objects are also supported. No structure or glycan-type metadata is required.

weight

Either "equal" (default) or "abundance". Equal weighting counts distinct compositions, or distinct combinations of protein, protein_site, and composition for glycoproteomics. Abundance weighting sums raw, linear-scale abundances across all rows and samples, including duplicate measurements. Missing abundances are omitted; negative and infinite values and recorded non-raw scales are rejected.

...

Common appearance options described in glyvis_plot_options.

Value

A tidyplot, also inheriting from ggplot, with category, value, and proportion in its data. All four categories are retained, including zero-valued categories. Proportions use the total eligible count or abundance as the denominator.

Details

Categories are ordered as Fuc+, Sia+, Fuc+, Sia-, Fuc-, Sia+, and Fuc-, Sia-. Fucose is inferred from dHex (including concrete Fuc); sialic acid includes both NeuAc and NeuGc. Counts greater than zero indicate presence. This does not distinguish core from antennal fucose. Each sector is annotated with its Fuc/Sia category and percentage. Missing compositions are excluded with a warning. Invalid compositions raise an error. Equal weighting counts annotations regardless of assay missingness. No sample-wise normalization is applied. Empty eligible input and non-positive total abundance raise an error.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("glyrepr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  plot_fuc_sia_pie(glyexp::real_experiment2)
}
